purpose: for the reading of Murāri Giri (murāreḥ pāṭhārthaṃ)
notes: The scribe's name is written 'jagyanātha', a spoken form of Yajñanātha. The cataloguer corrected it to Yajñanātha, which matches the catalogue field. 'yajñanāthayoḥ śubhaṃ bhūyāt' is a dual genitive, which is odd. It may be a scribal error for the singular yajñanāthasya, or it may mean two people (Yajña and Nātha?). It is taken here as the scribe alone. 'girir iti sunāmnaḥ' most likely means that Murāri carried the Daśanāmī name Giri, but this is inferred. The verse 'sukhaṃ gopālenāvataritamahśaṃkarakṣataṃ' is corrupt. Gopāla might be an earlier copyist, the composer of the verse, or a word play (an epithet of Kṛṣṇa), so this entry has low confidence. 'samayanāma' before Bhādramāse is unclear: perhaps a corrupt year name, or meaning 'in the month named'. 'pūrṇavāśyāyāṃ' is read as pūrṇamāsyām. The weekday (Friday) was not checked against an ephemeris. VS 1833 Bhādrapada falls in August/September 1776 CE. The closing verse 'dheyaṃ sadā ... mahāpurukha te caraṇāraviṃdaṃ' is a quoted stotra verse (Bhāgavata 11.5.33) and contains no persons.
